fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Circular Driveway; Water Feature; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Water Feature; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly on both sides, as the single access point must be immediately visible to arriving units.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the long driveway to maintain a clear travel path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back any tree branches overhanging the driveway to allow full-height clearance for fire apparatus and ambulances.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles so arriving units can reach the residence without stopping to reposition.
• Mark the boundary of the water feature nearest the driveway or turnaround area so responders working in low-light or smoky conditions do not approach it unknowingly.
• Designate and mark a flat staging area away from the water feature where responders can position equipment and personnel.
• Use the circular driveway as the primary turnaround point and keep it free of vehicles, decorative objects, and stored items at all times.
• Post a simple diagram of the property layout, including the detached structure location and circular driveway, at the road entrance or on a weatherproof box near the driveway entry.
• Confirm the detached structure has a visible address or unit identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Brush Area; Brush Area; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Single Access Route; Open Terrain; Water Feature; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim all shrubs that are growing directly next to the house so there is open ground between the plants and the walls.
• Remove or cut back brush in the areas immediately surrounding the structure to create open, clear ground around the building.
• Thin scattered shrubs within the yard to increase the open space between individual plants and the house.
• Clear brush from both sides of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without vegetation contact and so the route stays open during an emergency.
• Trim any tree branches that hang over or touch the house, roof, or deck.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not touch each other or extend over the building.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the mixed vegetation areas closest to the structure.
• Keep the driveway free of fallen branches, overgrown shrubs, and other debris along its full length.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the road.
• Maintain the single access route by keeping vegetation cut back on both sides from the road to the house.
• Move any cut brush, wood piles, or loose yard debris away from the house and outbuildings.
• Keep vegetation thinned and low in the open terrain areas closest to the structure so fire has less material to carry toward the building.
• Keep the area around the water feature clear of accumulated dead
